title: The Price of Not Wavering
description:
The last year.

Two years ago around this time, there was a day {name} nearly cracked under the weight. He pushed his own way through to the end instead.

Looking back now — whether that was right or wrong, the result will decide. But one thing was clear: someone who didn't waver has, at least, nothing to explain to himself.

choices.text: Go my own way to the end
choices.result_text: There's something only those who endured understand. Not pride, exactly — but not regret either. {name} started the last year the same way.

choices.text: Honestly, it scared him a little now
choices.result_text: The thought flickered — maybe pushing to the end had just been stubbornness. But it was too far to turn back. {name} let the thought go.

title: The Price of Turning
description:
The last year.

Two years ago, under the weight, {name} changed direction once. The straight-and-narrow type let in some risk; the risk-taker added a safety net.

Back then it felt like wavering, and that was embarrassing. Now he sees — it wasn't wavering, it was adjusting. Not trusting himself too much. That saved something.

choices.text: Being flexible is what protected me
choices.result_text: No telling how it'd have gone, locked onto one road. Knowing when to turn brought {name} this far. If that's a skill, it was a skill.

choices.text: Wondered for a second if he'd have earned more without turning
choices.result_text: The road not taken always looks better. {name} knew that. Without turning, he wouldn't have slept. Sleep is an asset too.

title: The Bill He Chose to Pay
description:
Two years ago, {name} saw the bill and folded it anyway. He knew the cost going in, he'd said, and he'd see it through.

Two years have passed. The bill is thicker now. The face in the mirror, the people drifted away, the body put off.

With the end in sight — the moment comes to ask whether the cost was really worth it.

choices.text: Coming this far means the price is paid
choices.result_text: Regret is a luxury. {name} chose to think so. It's the final stretch. Stop now and everything paid loses its meaning.

choices.text: When it's all over, reclaim what was lost, one by one
choices.result_text: Reach the goal or not, there's an after — {name} pictured it for the first time. That the end might not be the end was, somehow, a small comfort.

title: The Weight of What Was Reclaimed
description:
Two years ago, {name} decided to reclaim one of the things lost. The put-off call, the put-off checkup, the put-off person.

That small decision grew quietly over those two years. A reconnected relationship, a body looked after. He chased the goal but never let go of that thread.

Starting the last year now, {name} knows how lucky that was.

choices.text: Keeping balance is what held me up
choices.result_text: Not betting everything wasn't a weakness — it was strength. {name} knows that now. Those who chase only money arrive alone. {name} wasn't alone.

choices.text: Still, give the last year everything
choices.result_text: What needed reclaiming was reclaimed. Now the final sprint. {name} picked up the pace again — without letting the thread go.

title: After the Cut
description:
Last year, {name} cut off a cracked relationship. Not out of resolve — out of exhaustion.

After that, the door for letting people in got a little heavier. Safer, and narrower for it. In the last year, counting who was left beside him, {name} paused for a moment.

choices.result_text: A few proven people was enough. {name} settled it that way. Loneliness is a cost; betrayal is a loss. The cost is better.

choices.text: Maybe open the door again, for just one person
choices.result_text: Cutting off was easy; reopening was hard. Still, {name} stared at one contact a long while. Because someone who only ever closes doors ends up alone.

title: After Choosing to Understand
description:
Last year, {name} chose not to cut off the cracked relationship, but to understand it — even thinking he might be a sucker for it.

A year on — the person hadn't changed. But {name} had learned how to live without hating them. Maybe he took a loss. Still, his heart was light.

choices.text: Living on the side of trusting people is right
choices.result_text: Living in suspicion wrecks a person more than being used does. {name} chose to believe that. So what if you take a loss. You sleep well.

choices.text: This time, he drew a line
choices.result_text: Understanding and accepting everything are different. {name} knows that boundary now. Trust, but don't hand over everything. The year taught him that too.

title: Exactly That Much Distance
description:
Last year, {name} neither cut off nor held on to the person who'd cracked. He kept exactly that much distance.

That distance somehow became the default for every relationship. With everyone, just enough. Only as much as won't hurt. In the last year, {name} couldn't tell if that was comfort or loneliness.

choices.text: This distance is the adult way
choices.result_text: No expectation, no disappointment. {name} survived four years on that formula. It was efficient. Sometimes so efficient it frightened him.

choices.text: With one person, decided to close the gap
choices.result_text: No need to keep everyone at arm's length. {name} picked one and stepped closer. He might get hurt. But living only to avoid hurt, you end up with nothing.

title: Opening One Slot Again
description:
Last year, {name} sent a person or clinic he had missed two times he could actually keep instead of writing ‘any time.’ Only the sent time on his side remained on the screen. The earlier wait did not disappear.

In the final year, someone—a junior, perhaps, or an old friend—had missed a commitment and was editing the same apology over and over. {name} remembered putting forward a time he could keep instead of repeating the word sorry.

Now he had to decide whether to offer one slot from his side again.

choices.text: Send two times I can actually keep first
choices.result_text:
{name} did not write ‘any time.’ He sent two hours he could truly clear plus the travel time. Only a sent time remained beneath his bubble.

No read receipt, reply, or confirmed time appeared. He locked no appointment into the calendar. The only record he could verify was that he had made the first offer.

choices.text: It's the last year. Had to look after myself first.
choices.result_text:
There was no room. {name} left the input field open and moved to the next appointment. No one was there to label the choice wrong.

For a moment he remembered the two times he had sent last year and their sent time. This screen held neither a new offer nor a time of refusal.
